title: G1 C1 · Energy and its Uses

questions.q: Define energy.
questions.explain: Energy is the capacity to do work. The rate of energy conversion is power, and a push or a pull is a force.

questions.q: State the SI unit of energy.
questions.explain: The SI unit of energy is the joule (J). The watt is the unit of power and the newton is the unit of force.

questions.q: A ball rolls along the floor. Name the energy the moving ball has.
questions.explain: Any moving object has kinetic energy. The rolling ball is moving, so it has kinetic energy.

questions.q: Four identical balls roll along a floor. Identify the ball with the most kinetic energy.
questions.explain: Kinetic energy increases with speed. These balls are identical, so the fastest ball, at 8 m/s, has the most kinetic energy.

questions.q: Name the energy stored in a stretched rubber band.
questions.explain: A stretched or squashed elastic object stores elastic potential energy. The stretched rubber band stores this energy until it is let go.

questions.q: Name the energy stored in food and fuels.
questions.explain: Food and fuels store chemical potential energy. This energy is released when food is digested or a fuel is burnt.

questions.q: Name the energy an object has because of its height.
questions.explain: An object raised above the ground has gravitational potential energy. The higher the object, the more gravitational potential energy it has.

questions.q: Identify the object that stores elastic potential energy.
choices: a car moving along a road
questions.explain: A compressed spring is squashed out of its normal shape, so it stores elastic potential energy. Rice and a battery store chemical potential energy, and a moving car has kinetic energy.

questions.q: A lift moves in a tall building. Identify where it has the most gravitational potential energy.
questions.explain: Gravitational potential energy increases with height. The lift is highest at the top floor, so it has the most gravitational potential energy there.

questions.q: An object has thermal energy because of one property. State this property.
questions.explain: Thermal energy depends on temperature. A hotter object has more thermal energy than the same object when it is cooler.

questions.q: State the direction in which thermal energy is transferred.
questions.explain: Thermal energy always moves from a hotter region to a cooler region. It does not depend on the size or mass of the objects.

questions.q: A bottle of hot milk is placed in cold water. Predict what happens to the milk.
choices: it takes in cold from water
questions.explain: The hot milk is hotter than the cold water, so thermal energy moves from the milk to the water. The milk loses thermal energy and cools down. Cold is not something that moves.

questions.q: State the Principle of the Conservation of Energy.
choices: energy cannot be created or destroyed
energy cannot be stored or released
energy can be used up completely
energy cannot be changed or transferred
questions.explain: The Principle of the Conservation of Energy states that energy cannot be created or destroyed. It can only change from one form to another.

questions.q: Energy changes from one form to another. Predict the total energy after the change.
questions.explain: Energy cannot be created or destroyed. When energy changes form, the total amount of energy stays the same as before.

questions.q: A television is switched on. Identify the main energy conversion.
questions.explain: A television uses electrical energy. Its screen gives out light energy and its speakers give out sound energy.

questions.q: A candle burns. Identify the energy conversion.
questions.explain: Candle wax stores chemical potential energy. When the candle burns, this energy changes into heat and light.

questions.q: A battery is used to light a torch. Identify the energy conversion in the battery.
questions.explain: A battery stores chemical potential energy. When it is used, the battery changes this energy into electrical energy for the torch.

questions.q: A person sings into a microphone. Identify the energy conversion in the microphone.
questions.explain: A microphone takes in sound energy and changes it into electrical energy. A loudspeaker does the opposite change.

questions.q: A generator in a power station spins. Identify the energy conversion in the generator.
questions.explain: A generator is turned by a spinning turbine. It changes this kinetic energy into electrical energy.

questions.q: Identify the activity that changes electrical energy into chemical potential energy.
questions.explain: Charging a phone battery stores the electrical energy as chemical potential energy in the battery. Burning charcoal and roasting change energy into heat, and a fan changes electrical energy into kinetic energy.

questions.q: A radio uses 200 J. 50 J becomes heat, the rest sound. Calculate the sound energy.
questions.explain: Energy is conserved, so the energy out equals the energy in. Sound energy = 200 J - 50 J = 150 J.

questions.q: A lamp gives out 300 J light and 700 J heat. Calculate the energy supplied.
questions.explain: Energy is conserved, so the energy supplied equals all the energy given out. Energy supplied = 300 J + 700 J = 1000 J.

questions.q: A ball thrown up has 100 J kinetic energy. State its potential energy at the top.
questions.explain: As the ball rises, its kinetic energy changes into gravitational potential energy. At the top it stops for a moment, so all 100 J has become potential energy.

questions.q: A swing moves from its highest point to its lowest point. Identify the energy change.
questions.explain: At its highest point the swing has the most gravitational potential energy. As it falls to its lowest point, this changes into kinetic energy.

questions.q: A child swings freely on a swing. Identify where the kinetic energy is greatest.
questions.explain: The swing is lowest and fastest at the bottom of its path. All its gravitational potential energy has changed into kinetic energy there, so its kinetic energy is greatest at the lowest point.

questions.q: Define power.
choices: the energy stored in a fuel
questions.explain: Power is the rate of energy conversion. It tells us how much energy is converted every second.

questions.q: State the SI unit of power.
questions.explain: The SI unit of power is the watt (W). One watt is one joule of energy converted every second.

questions.q: State the formula for power in terms of energy and time.
questions.explain: Power is the energy converted divided by the time taken. So power = energy ÷ time.

questions.q: P is power, E is energy and t is time. Identify the formula for time.
questions.explain: Rearranging P = E ÷ t gives t = E ÷ P. Time is the energy divided by the power.

questions.q: A boy uses 800 J of energy in 4 s. Calculate his power.
questions.explain: Power = energy ÷ time = 800 J ÷ 4 s = 200 W.

questions.q: A fan uses 900 J of energy in 3 s. Calculate its power.
questions.explain: Power = energy ÷ time = 900 J ÷ 3 s = 300 W.

questions.q: An activity lasts 2 minutes. Calculate this time in seconds.
questions.explain: One minute is 60 seconds. So 2 minutes = 2 × 60 s = 120 s.

questions.q: A heater has a power of 2 kW. Calculate its power in watts.
questions.explain: One kilowatt is 1000 watts. So 2 kW = 2 × 1000 W = 2000 W.

questions.q: A 200 W oven is on for 10 s. Calculate the energy used.
questions.explain: Energy = power × time = 200 W × 10 s = 2000 J.

questions.q: A 50 W lamp uses 1000 J of energy. Calculate the time taken.
questions.explain: Time = energy ÷ power = 1000 J ÷ 50 W = 20 s.
